column170: Dear Matt, Thank you for your consultation. Based on your pattern of loss, donor capacity, lifestyle, and long-term goals, I’ve prepared a tailored plan that prioritises natural results while preserving your donor for future needs. 1. Patient Summary Name: Matt Walker Age: 39 Occupation: Construction Pattern: Grade 5 Male Pattern Baldness Donor: Limited reserve — requires conservative, strategic graft planning Medication: Finasteride (alternate days recommended until age 45) Transition to Saw Palmetto thereafter Goals: Achieve a stronger frontal and midscalp appearance Maintain a masculine, age-appropriate design Preserve donor for possible future further crown density 2. Donor Preservation Strategy (Critical in Grade 5 MPB) Your donor area is limited, which is common in Grade 5 patterns. The priority is to: Maximise impact where it matters most visually the frontal and midscalp regions, covergae in crown Avoid over-harvesting to protect your ability to add crown density later if needed. Use PTT (Partial Transection Technique) This allows partial follicle retention, ensuring: Stem cells remain behind in the donor Higher long-term donor regeneration Safer extractions with reduced trauma Sustainable graft numbers for future correction This approach is the safest way to manage limited donor resources. 3. Medical Therapy Plan A. Finasteride (Alternate Days Until 45) This keeps DHT levels suppressed and prevents acceleration of midscalp and crown thinning. Why alternate days? Still provides strong DHT control Reduces long-term exposure while maintaining stability Ideal for patients planning to transition off medication later in life B. Transition to Saw Palmetto at Age 45 Once past 45, your hormonal decline naturally reduces DHT activity. Saw Palmetto becomes a safe, natural way to: Maintain existing stability Support crown and midscalp hair Avoid pharmaceutical use long-term Reduce inflammation and improve hair quality 4. Surgical Plan – Frontal & Midscalp Priority Primary Focus Rebuild frontal hairline Reinforce midscalp Create a natural density gradient to blend into the crown Maintain the option for future crown refinement if donor allows Why Not Crown First? The frontal region provides 80% of a person's visual density and appearance. The crown is a larger surface area and requires thousands of grafts for full coverage — not suitable with a limited donor. By preserving grafts now, we open the possibility of addressing the crown later. Technique Used PTT (Partial Transection Technique) Maximises donor regeneration Reduces visible thinning in the donor Critical for patients with limited reserves DFI Implantation Allows precise angle and direction control Moderate density placement to maximise coverage Natural blending front → midscalp → crown transition 5. Regenerative Support Included Exosomes Applied on Surgery Day To enhance graft survival and support the miniaturised surrounding hairs: Boost cellular signalling Improve collagen remodelling Accelerate early growth phases Reduce inflammation and improve shedding cycles PRP Therapy – 3 Sessions Post-Op PRP helps stabilise weak hairs in the midscalp and crown, especially important with limited donor supply. Benefits include: Thickening of native hairs Faster post-operative recovery Improved overall density appearance Extending the longevity of your result 6. Total Cost 2 Day Session (as determined clinically) – $15,000 AUD Includes: PTT extraction DFI implantation Exosomes on the day PRP on the day + 3 PRP sessions post-op Consultation reviews and post-care Donor management and long-term planning Payment Options: Release My Super: https://lp.releasemysuper.au/evolvedhair Humm90: https://apply.flexicards.com.au/seller=EVHRS 7. Expected Outcome With strategic donor management and regenerative support, you can expect: A stronger, fuller-looking frontal hairline Balanced density through the midscalp A natural transition into the crown Improved overall thickness from PRP + Exosomes Donor preservation for potential future crown work Long-term stability with Finasteride → Saw Palmetto plan Matt, this is the safest and most effective pathway to rebuild your appearance while ensuring your donor remains viable for any future crown needs. Please let me know if you'd like to book your surgery date or discuss any part of your plan.
